what: every block of both stacks, as a share of the model's squared gradient norm. Summed directly from bundle_min_043/grads_f64_043.pt on qb2 (4,170 tensors, model total 10.279642678524986, sha256 1d4ea922...). CPU only, no device opened. Exhaustive: the 17 top-level sections sum to 100.0 % over all 4,170 tensors.
basis: upstream OpenFold3 0.4.3, 4,170 parameters. NOT the 0.5.0 / 4,147 basis that pass 91 disqualified -- every share on that basis is a share of a model we do not claim.
headline: The sixteen highest-mass blocks in the whole model are all diffusion-transformer blocks. DiT block 8 alone is 9.84053 % of the model -- 1.69x the entire 48-block pairformer stack (5.8282 %), and 9.2x pairformer block 47 (1.06624 %), the block this campaign has investigated most deeply. No block-scope arm has ever been run on DiT block 8.
dit_shape: front-loaded and then it collapses. Blocks 0-15 hold 43.1946 % of the model; blocks 16-23 hold 0.6990 % -- the last third of the diffusion transformer is seven tenths of one percent of the gradient mass. A depth ladder that samples the DiT uniformly spends a third of its runs on 1.6 % of what it is measuring.
pairformer_shape: flat at ~0.05-0.18 % for 46 blocks, then a two-block spike: block 46 is 0.42818 % and block 47 is 1.06624 %, 8.4x block 0. Those two blocks are 25.6 % of the whole trunk's mass. Block 47 was picked for this campaign because it was the WORST-PERFORMING block; it also happens to be the heaviest, which the campaign did not know when it picked it.

corrects_on_the_record.the inversion that matters: on the old basis aux_heads (4.27) read LARGER than the whole pairformer trunk (3.156). Measured, pairformer is 5.8282 % and aux_heads 2.8431 % -- pairformer is 2.05x larger. The ordering flips.

what_this_does_not_establish: this is mass, not error. A block holding 9.84 % of the gradient can be perfectly ported and a block holding 0.017 % can be badly wrong. Mass says where a given amount of error COSTS most, and therefore where an arm is worth building; it is not itself a parity result. It is also one batch (batch_step003, 5nw3, 56 real tokens) at one r = 0 step -- nothing here shows these shares are stable across batches.
